name: Arab & Berber Souks
hero_subtitle: Two complementary markets in the medina of Taroudant, the Little Marrakech — silver, leather, spices and daily life.

overview.title: Markets that still serve the town
overview.p1: Taroudant has two main market areas often called the Arab souk and the Berber (Amazigh) souk. They sit close to Place Assarag and remain working markets as much as visitor attractions.
overview.p2: Expect silver jewellery, leather goods, spices, argan products, textiles and everyday produce. Bargaining is expected but usually calmer than in high-pressure tourist streets.
overview.p3: Use Place Assarag as your landmark: from the square you can step into either market, then return for tea before diving back in.

q1.question: Is Arab & Berber Souks free to visit?
q1.answer: In most cases public areas are free. Confirm any ticketed interiors on site.

q2.question: How long should I spend?
q2.answer: Thirty minutes to two hours depending on the site and your pace.

q3.question: What is the best time to go?
q3.answer: Morning or late afternoon for cooler temperatures and better light.

q4.question: How do I get there from the medina?
q4.answer: On foot if central, or by petit taxi. Ask for the place name as a landmark.

q5.question: Can I take photos?
q5.answer: Usually yes outdoors. Ask before photographing people or restricted interiors.
